findings.passage: “Arizona is proud to stand with Idaho and any state that chooses to enact reasonable protections like voter ID,” said Speaker Montenegro. “Student IDs vary widely in design and security features. States have every right to require more reliable documentation to ensure only eligible voters are casting ballots.”
findings.note: Official House news release announcing an amicus brief that supports Idaho's voter ID law, which does not accept student ID cards at the polls.

findings.passage: “Arizona’s election laws are under constant attack by activists who want to chip away at basic security measures. If we don’t fight back, we risk undermining public confidence in our elections,” Speaker Montenegro added. “Every eligible voter should be able to vote—and every illegal vote must be prevented.”
findings.note: Same release; general statement on election security laws and defending them in court.

findings.passage: “Common-sense measures will better secure our elections, like government-issued photo ID for in-person voting, banning unsupervised ballot drop boxes & more. Hopefully, our Governor respects the will of the people and joins us, but we can always take these improvements directly to the voters if we must.”
findings.note: Breitbart quotes a post he wrote on the Friday before its 2024-11-23 report, when he was Speaker-elect. He backs photo ID for in-person voting and sending such measures to voters.
subjects: taking election measures to the ballot

findings.passage: “Another area of elections we can and should improve deals with signature verification. Stronger Voter ID requirements for absentee ballots can speed and better secure the process. Growing support for this in the State House.”
findings.note: Second post quoted in the same Breitbart report; he calls for stronger voter ID requirements for absentee ballots.

findings.passage: “Arizonans expect elections to be run according to the law, not rewritten to fit the Secretary of State’s partisan agenda,” said Montenegro. “Secretary Fontes’ draft manual again contradicts Arizona statutes, weakens safeguards against non-citizen voting, undermines legislative authority, and even pressures election officers to surrender their constitutional rights. Such abuses erode trust in our elections and will not stand.”
findings.note: Statement quoted by the Arizona Daily Independent (page dated 2025-09-06) about his letter objecting to the draft 2025 Elections Procedures Manual, including provisions on registrations without ID numbers and on proof-of-citizenship challenges.
